notes: ModernBERT-Ja-310M Decision (mlboydaisuke/ModernBERT-Ja-310M-Decision-LiteRT, Hub revision fbe068f32fe6360639eaf083b0b30bfc4637a46f, published 2026-10-02; source argos1111/modernbert-ja-310m-jev rev 07cda235, CC BY-SA 4.0, a Japanese ModernBertForSequenceClassification cross-encoder: 25 layers, hidden 768, global attention every third layer, sliding window 128). One (question + state, candidate) pair -> one logit; the host applies softmax over a question's candidates (choice / score / noul). Inputs inputs_embeds [1,N,768] (host token-table lookup, fp16 table 102400x768) and attention_mask [1,N]; output logit [1,1,1,1]; one graph call per candidate (latency_p50_ms = per PAIR, write + run + readback). wfp16 storage: the 102 FULLY_CONNECTED weights float16 + DEQUANTIZE, everything else float32 (1,911 operators). The shipped graphs carry two fp32-exact rewrites (mask constant -1e4; SafeLayerNorm 2^-k with k 5-6 in layers 14-24, 2 on the final norm) so fp16 computation is finite everywhere, but fp16 computation still moves answers (Mac Metal default precision 619/621 winners; see the GPU default-precision / FP16 rows). GpuOptions(precision = FP32) is the validated GPU setting. artifact_sha256 = the Hub LFS sha256 (API siblings.lfs, read 2026-10-02), equal to the local export's sha256 verified after upload (scripts/verify_remote.py). Reference for parity = the card's own transformers snippet (transformers 5.17.0, the author's version) on CPU fp32 over 547 fixture requests (JGLUE v1.3 test 250 JNLI + 250 JCommonsenseQA, the author's 16 items and 12-question example, 30 invented Japanese requests; 621 questions, 2,357 pairs, 123 boundary). Lane record: ~/code/standup/handoffs/2026-10-02-modernbert-ja-decision-litert.md; run dir /Users/USER/code/codex-conversions/2026-10-02/modernbert-ja-decision-litert. The unpublished rank-4 BATCH_MATMUL twin (`_r4`, S26 GPU FP32 621/621 at S512) is not a record (#174(3)). Window N=256: the 546 of 547 fixture requests whose pairs fit 256 tokens (618 questions, 120 boundary, 2,348 pairs); every row ran on an already hot phone (thermal status 2-3, 44.8-47 C) after the S512 GPU run. The NPU rows are the PUBLISHED graph (JIT 29.5 s first compile; 0.5 s from the cache on the float32-table repeat): every winning candidate kept, the same one question at 0.0113 with either host table, so the table rounding is not the cause.
